message.what: Geomagnetic activity has reached the G5 (Extreme) level.
message.observed: G5 conditions were observed at 2058 UTC during the 2100-2400 UTC observation period.
message.basis: This alert is based on 12/13 real-time observations from the official Kp magnetometer network available at the time of issuance.
message.current_status: A Space Weather Warning remains in effect.
message.future_alerts: This is the first and only G5 Observed Space Weather Alert that will be issued for this event. Continued major storm conditions will be communicated through Warning Updates.
message.impacts: Power systems may experience widespread voltage-control issues, increased geomagnetically induced currents, and protective system concerns. HF radio communication may be degraded or unavailable over some paths. GNSS users may experience degraded accuracy, loss of lock, or other performance issues in disturbed ionospheric regions. Low-Earth-orbit satellites may experience significantly increased drag. Aurora may be visible much farther south than usual if local sky conditions allow.
message.precautionary_preparedness_actions: Partners should follow sector-specific procedures for extreme geomagnetic activity. Power grid, aviation, satellite, GNSS, and HF radio users should maintain heightened situational awareness and monitor SWPC Warning Updates, Space Weather Summaries, and decision-support guidance.
